The 2022 revelation that a subcontractor for the F-35 program had sourced cobalt (for use in the aircraft’s pump magnets) from China (Clark 2022) highlights how a lack of supply chain visibility can permeate DOW programs. Expanding supply chain resilience could be achieved by: • Conducting reviews on key military equipment and assets to determine where supply chain transparency is lacking, from raw materials to transport (Helton 2021) • Using integrated supply chain models that consider competition with the private sector and other nations to focus on key vulnerabilities and improve stockpiling plans 20 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Collaborating with stakeholders and utilities to proactively manage supply chain risks • Employing long-term contracts to encourage onshoring or friendshoring of mining, refining, manufacturing, or recycling • Working with industry to improve software and firmware supply chain transparency. 6.4 Workforce Development More structured approaches to hiring and skills development could help DOW deploy and maintain advanced energy technologies. Simply hiring more contractors would likely be insufficient, given that some missions, such as cyber, require experts who are able to deploy. Efforts could include: • Creating a formal talent pipeline, including structured recruitment and training programs in collaboration with educational institutions, ensuring a steady flow of skilled workers • Expanding interdisciplinary training for IT and OT professionals, including cross- disciplinary education and certifications • Adaptable workforce development plans that cater to mission and technology-specific needs (President’s National Infrastructure Advisory Council 2021). For example, to mitigate the risk of losing institutional cyber knowledge due to personnel turnover, identify cyber talent requirements that demand deployment-ready members, and those that are better suited for contracted personnel. 6.5 Exercises and Simulations Expanding the scope and depth of DOW’s simulations and exercises could help address the risks outlined throughout this analysis. By simulating the behavior of advanced energy technologies under stress (i.e., considering weather extremes, different physical environments, interoperability challenges, and logistics requirements), DOW can identify vulnerabilities and refine energy resilience strategies.
